verification.notes: Section XVIII: after Dasharatha's horse-sacrifice, Kausalya gives birth to Rama, described as the eldest and eating half the sacrificial payasa portion given to her.
Section XVIII: Sumitra, having eaten two portions of the sacrificial payasa, gives birth to twins Lakshmana and Shatrughna.
Section XVIII: Sumitra gives birth to both Lakshmana and Shatrughna as twins after the horse-sacrifice.
Section XVIII: Kausalya is named as the queen who bears Dasharatha's eldest son Rama, identifying her as his wife.
Section XVIII: Sumitra is named as Dasharatha's queen who bears Lakshmana and Shatrughna.
Section XVIII: Vasishtha, the royal family priest, performs the naming ceremony for all four princes including Bharata, and is elsewhere their household preceptor.
Section XVIII: Vasishtha, the royal family priest, performs the naming ceremony for all four princes including Shatrughna, and is elsewhere their household preceptor.

note.en: Manthara is Kaikeyi's hump-backed nurse and maidservant, whose counsel turns Kaikeyi against Rama's installation as heir-apparent.

verification.notes: Section VII: Manthara, described as a maidservant raised alongside Kaikeyi, serves as her personal nurse/attendant and is the one who incites her against Rama's installation.

note.en: Kaikeyi once saved Dasharatha's life in battle against the Asura Timidhvaja, earning the two boons she later invokes to secure Bharata's throne and Rama's exile.

verification.notes: Section IX: Manthara reminds Kaikeyi that she once saved Dasharatha's life on the battlefield against the Asura Samvara/Timidhvaja, for which he granted her two boons -- later claimed as Bharata's installation and Rama's exile.
Section V: the sage lists the offspring begotten by Sumali on Ketumati, naming Prahasta, Dhumraksha, and Kaikasi (Kaikesi) of luminous smiles among them.
Section V: Kaikasi (Kaikesi) is named among the children Sumali begot on his wife Ketumati.
Section V: Prahasta is listed first among the offspring Sumali begot on Ketumati.
Section V: Prahasta is named among the children born of Sumali and Ketumati.
Section V: Prahasta and Kaikasi (Kaikesi) are both listed as offspring of the same parents, Sumali and Ketumati, making them siblings.
Section V: Dhumraksha is listed among the offspring Sumali begot on Ketumati.
Section V: Dhumraksha is named among the children born of Sumali and Ketumati.
Section LXVIII: Rakshasas report to Ravana that Kumbhakarna has met his quietus at the hands of Rama, his body mutilated and lying at Lanka's gate.
Yuddha XCI carries the Aindra weapon and the beheading; XC only opens the duel.
Section XVII: while Vali and Sugriva grapple in single combat, Rama looses a serpent-like shaft from concealment that strikes Vali's breast and fells him.
Section IX: Sumali sends his daughter Kaikasi (Kaikesi) to the ascetic Vishrava (Vicrava), son of Pulastya, and she takes him for her lord, becoming the mother of his Rakshasa children.
Section IX: after her union with Vishrava, Kaikasi brings forth the ten-necked offspring who is named Ravana by his father.
Section IX: 'After him was born Kumbhakarna,' Kaikasi's second son by Vishrava, born after Ravana.
Section IX: the text states 'the righteous Bibhishana is the youngest son of Kaikasi,' naming him last among her children by Vishrava.
Section IX: Vibhishana is born to Kaikasi as the youngest of the children she bears to Vishrava, alongside Ravana, Kumbhakarna, and Surpanakha.
Section LXVI: the Wind embraces Anjana and tells her she shall bear a son equal to him in strength and leaping; the narrator confirms 'thou art the son of the Wind, my child.'
Section LXVI: Anjana, embraced by the Wind-god, gives birth to Hanuman in a mountain cave.

note.en: Hanuman is reckoned the son of the vanara Kesari by Anjana, and also the son of Vayu the Wind-god, who begot him on her by divine embrace.

verification.notes: Section LXVI: the text calls Hanuman 'the son of Kesari by his wife' Anjana, naming Kesarin as his father alongside the Wind-god's divine paternity.
Section XXXIX: during Vali's circuit of the four oceans carrying the captured Ravana under his arm, the text names him 'Vali, the son of Indra, and the king of monkeys.'

note.en: Vali once caught Ravana, who had come to fight him, and carried him helpless under his arm across the four oceans before releasing him at Kishkindha.

verification.notes: Section XXXIX: Vali seizes Ravana, who comes to challenge him, tucks him under his arm, and carries him on a tour of the four oceans while performing his prayers, before releasing him humiliated at Kishkindha.
Section VII: Vasishtha and Vamadeva are named as Dasharatha's two family priests (purohitas), the foremost among his counsellors.

note.en: When Indrajit's weapon fells Rama and Lakshmana and panic seizes the vanara army, Vibhishana steadies Sugriva and rallies the monkey forces at his side.

verification.notes: Section XLVI: when Rama and Lakshmana lie stricken by Indrajit's serpent-shafts and Sugriva is overcome with fear, Vibhishana comforts him, washes his eyes, and rallies him and the panicked monkey troops.
Section LI: after a long aerial duel in which Jatayu shatters Ravana's bow, chariot, and shield, Ravana draws his dagger and cuts off Jatayu's wings, legs, and sides, felling him mortally.
Section XXII: 'Angada, Tara's son, gifted with energy and strength, shall perform...' -- Angada is repeatedly identified through the kanda as Tara's son by Vali.

note.en: Jambavan serves as elder counsellor to the young Angada during the search for Sita, and it is his counsel that turns the mission over to Hanuman.

verification.notes: Section LXV: when the search party despairs at Sampati's cliff, Jambavan counsels Angada on the wisdom of persevering and, with Angada's backing, directs Hanuman to make the leap to Lanka.
Section XII: the Danava Maya, learning Ravana is Pulastya's descendant, gives his daughter Mandodari -- born to him by the Apsara Hema -- to Ravana in marriage.

note.en: Ravana defeats his half-brother Kubera in single combat, drives him out, and takes his flying chariot Pushpaka as the trophy of conquest.

verification.notes: Section XV: Ravana attacks his half-brother Kubera (Vaishravana), fells him with a mace-blow, drives him from Lanka and Kailasa, and seizes his Pushpaka chariot as the spoil of victory.
Section LVIII: the vanara general Nila duels Ravana's commander-in-chief Prahasta and finally crushes his head with a hurled crag, killing him outright.
Section CXIV: at Rama's command, Lakshmana sprinkles Vibhishana with ocean water and installs him as king of Lanka before the assembled Rakshasas.

note.en: It is Lakshmana who performs Vibhishana's coronation as king of Lanka, sprinkling him with ocean water at Rama's command.

verification.notes: Section CXIV: Lakshmana personally performs the coronation rite, sprinkling Vibhishana with sea-water and installing him as king of Lanka at Rama's direction.
Section XX: fleeing the ruin of the fourteen Rakshasas Khara sent after Rama, Surpanakha runs weeping to Khara, and the text names her explicitly 'the sister of Khara.'
Section XXX: in single combat before Janasthana, Rama looses a shaft that fells Khara dead to the earth, avenging Surpanakha's mutilation-driven war-party.
Section XXVII: Rama duels the three-headed Rakshasa Trishira, wounds him with fourteen arrows, and finally severs his three heads with three shafts, killing him.

Section CX: Ravana falls in the final duel; the text states 'Ravana, the dread of all people, being slain' and that 'slaying that foremost of the Rakshasas, Rama satisfied the desire of Sugriva, Angada and Bibhishana.'

note.en: Despite fighting on Rama's side against him, Vibhishana mourns Ravana as his brother and personally performs his funeral rites after the war.

verification.notes: Section CXI: Vibhishana laments over his slain brother's body and, at Rama's word that their enmity has ended with death, asks leave to perform Ravana's funeral obsequies himself.

note.en: Rishyasringa presides as officiating sage over Dasharatha's son-giving sacrifice, which the tradition credits with the birth of Rama and his brothers.

verification.notes: Section XIII: Rishyasringa is brought to Ayodhya and, with the principal Brahmanas at his head, conducts Dasharatha's putrakameshti sacrifice for the birth of sons.

note.en: Vasishtha and Vishvamitra are rival sages whose feud over the wish-cow Sabala ends in reconciliation, Vasishtha himself confirming Vishvamitra's rank as Brahmarshi.

verification.notes: Section LXV: after their long feud over the wish-granting cow Sabala escalates into a war of curses and weapons, Vasishtha and Vishvamitra reconcile, with Vasishtha recognizing Vishvamitra as a true Brahmarshi.

note.en: Rama and Sugriva swear a fire-witnessed pact of friendship, promising to help each other -- Rama to kill Vali, Sugriva to help find Sita.

verification.notes: Section V: Rama and Sugriva clasp hands and walk around a fire kindled by Hanuman, sealing a formal vow of friendship and mutual aid.

note.en: Hanuman engineers Rama's first meeting with Sugriva and officiates the fire-rite that seals their alliance, becoming Rama's foremost devotee thereafter.

verification.notes: Section V: Hanuman first brings Rama and Sugriva together, then personally kindles and tends the sacrificial fire that witnesses their vow of friendship.

note.en: Brahma comes to reward Kumbhakarna with a boon but, fearing his hunger, has Saraswati twist his tongue so he asks for endless sleep instead of sovereignty.

verification.notes: Section X: Brahma comes to grant boons to Ravana's brothers; warned by the gods that Kumbhakarna would devour the three worlds, he has Saraswati sit on Kumbhakarna's tongue so he unwittingly asks only for long sleep instead of Indra's throne.
Section X: in the same visit, Brahma grants Vibhishana immortality for his righteousness despite his Rakshasa birth, immediately before turning to Kumbhakarna's boon.
Section X: at Brahma's request, Saraswati enters Kumbhakarna's throat and garbles his speech so that, meaning to ask for Indra's seat, he instead asks to sleep for many years.

note.en: Dutt renders the name as 'prince Aksha'; this is Akshayakumara, Ravana and Mandodari's son sent to fight Hanuman in the Ashoka garden, whom Hanuman kills by whirling him to the ground.

verification.notes: Section XLVII: Ravana's son, called 'prince Aksha' in this translation (the Akshayakumara of the wider tradition -- Ravana's youngest son sent against Hanuman in the Ashoka garden), attacks Hanuman and is whirled and dashed to death by him.
Section XLIV: after Jambumali falls to Hanuman's whirled sala-bolt, the text names him 'the mighty son of Prahasta.'
Section XLIV: Hanuman whirls an uprooted sala tree and lets it fall on Jambumali's breast, killing him instantly in the Ashoka garden fight.
Section XLVI: after Yupaksha and Virupaksha spring at him with maces, Hanuman uproots a sala tree and slays both Rakshasas with it.
Sundara XLVI carries Durdhara’s death; re-cited after audit.
Section XLVI: after Praghasa attacks him with an axe, Hanuman uproots a mountain-peak and crushes him along with Bhasakarna, killing both.
Section XLVI: Bhasakarna attacks Hanuman with a javelin and is crushed, together with Praghasa, beneath a mountain-peak Hanuman hurls at them.

note.en: Malyavan, Ravana's maternal grandsire and elder statesman among the Rakshasas, counsels him -- futilely -- to make peace with Rama and give Sita back.

verification.notes: Section XXXV: when Ravana asks his council for counsel against Rama, the text introduces the speaker as 'the maternal grand sire (of Ravana), named Malyavan,' who then urges Ravana to make peace and return Sita.

note.en: Shuka appears among Ravana's court officials, attending on the assembled Rakshasa lords alongside Prahasta.

verification.notes: Section XI: at Ravana's council convened over Vibhishana's counsel, Suka (Shuka) and Prahasta together attend to seating the assembled lords, marking Suka as one of Ravana's courtiers/ministers.
Section XXX: Ravana's spy Sardula, describing the vanara commanders to him, states 'Nila himself is the son of the bearer of sacrificial oblations' -- Agni, the fire-god.

note.en: Rama sends Angada as his envoy to Ravana's court to demand Sita's return; Ravana has him seized, but Angada breaks free and destroys a palace turret before flying back to Rama.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Book VI (Yuddha Kanda), Canto XLI: Rama's Envoy

verification.notes: Canto XLI: Rama sends Angada as his envoy into Ravana's court to deliver an ultimatum; Angada names himself 'Angad the son of Bali' before Ravana's guards seize him and he breaks free, wrecking a turret before returning to Rama's camp.
